title: 卜算子·我住长江头
title_en: Bu Suan Zi: I Live at the Head of the Yangtze
author: 李之仪

form.zh: 词，词牌《卜算子》，双调四十五字
form.en: ci to the tune Bu Suan Zi, 45 characters in two stanzas

readings.zh: “不”本来读 bù，在去声字“见”前面，口语里变读 bú。这里标本来的读音。
readings.en: The character bù is read bú in speech before a fourth-tone syllable like jiàn. Here we mark its basic tone.

readings.zh: “不”本来读 bù，在去声字“负”前面，口语里变读 bú。这里标本来的读音。
readings.en: The character bù is read bú in speech before a fourth-tone syllable like fù. Here we mark its basic tone.

glosses.en: cháng jiāng tóu: the upper part of the Yangtze River, near where it begins.
jūn: you, a polite way to address someone.
cháng jiāng wěi: the lower part of the Yangtze, near the sea.
gòng yǐn: drink together, drink the same water.

glosses.zh: 此恨：这份离别的痛苦。恨，这里是遗憾、痛苦的意思，不是仇恨。
glosses.en: cǐ hèn: this pain of being apart. Hèn here means sorrow and regret, not hatred.

glosses.zh: 不负：不辜负，不让对方失望。
相思意：互相思念的情意。
glosses.en: xiāng sī yì: the love of missing each other.

translation.en: I live at the head of the Yangtze,
and you live at its tail.
Every day I miss you but cannot see you,

translation.zh: 我们一起喝着同一条长江的水。
translation.en: yet we drink the water of the same river.

translation.zh: 这江水什么时候才会停止流淌？
translation.en: When will this river stop flowing?

translation.zh: 这离别的痛苦什么时候才会结束？
translation.en: When will this sorrow of parting end?

translation.zh: 只希望你的心像我的心一样，
translation.en: I only hope your heart is like mine,

translation.zh: 一定不会辜负我们互相思念的情意。
translation.en: and you will never let down our love for each other.

background.zh: 李之仪晚年被贬到太平州（今安徽当涂），那里就在长江边上。一般认为这首词是他在那里写的。一说是写给当地一位叫杨姝的歌女。词里用的都是很简单的话，像民歌一样，写的是一个人对远方心上人的思念。
background.en: In his later years, Li Zhiyi was sent away in disgrace to Taipingzhou (today's Dangtu, Anhui), right on the Yangtze. This lyric is usually thought to be written there. One account says it was written for a local singer named Yang Shu. The words are very simple, like a folk song. It tells of someone missing a loved one far away.

author_note.zh: 李之仪（约1048—约1117），北宋词人，号姑溪居士。他和苏轼是好朋友，做过苏轼的幕僚。后来因为得罪了权臣被贬官。他的词清新自然，这首《卜算子》是他最有名的作品。
author_note.en: Li Zhiyi (about 1048 to about 1117), also called the Retired Scholar of Guxi, was a Northern Song lyric poet. He was a good friend of Su Shi and once worked on his staff. Later he offended powerful officials and was demoted. His lyrics are fresh and natural, and this one is his most famous.

appreciation.zh: 这首词像一首民歌，句子简单，却很深情。一条长江，把两个人分在两头，离得很远；可是两个人喝的是同一条江的水，又好像连在一起。这一远一近，把思念写得又苦又甜。下阕说：江水不会停，我的思念也不会停。最后他不再抱怨，只希望对方的心和自己一样，不辜负这份感情。读这首词，可以想象一条长长的江，两头各站着一个人，望着同一片江水。
appreciation.en: This lyric is like a folk song: simple lines, deep feeling. One river puts two people at its two ends, far apart. Yet they drink the water of the same river, so they also seem joined. Far and near at once, the longing feels both bitter and sweet. The second stanza says the river will never stop, and neither will his longing. In the end he no longer complains. He only hopes the other heart is like his own and will stay true. As you read, picture a long, long river with one person at each end, both gazing at the same water.
